spans.s: Gośīrṣa, n. of a nāga king: Kv 〔2.12〕.
gośṛṅgavratin, a member of some heretical sect: Mvy 〔3542〕. Possibly cf. govratika ?
Gośṛṅgī, n. of a pious woman who entertained the Buddha: Mv 〔i.261.15〕; 〔263.3, 6〕; 〔271.13〕.

goṣṭhika (once written gau˚; not in this sense in Skt., but only as adj., relating to a guild; not in Pali; but = AMg. goṭṭhiya, ˚iga), m., usually pl., (boon-)companion, member of a friendly group: Mv 〔iii.375.13〕 triṃśa(d) goṣṭhikā udyānabhūmiṃ nirgatā; id. 15 and 〔376.1—2〕 tehi goṣṭhikehi; 〔376.5, 7, 8〕; Av 〔i.93.6〕; saṃbahulāś ca goṣṭhikā … 〔163.7〕; ˚kānāṃ śataṃ nirgataṃ 〔377.14〕; 〔ii.53.9 ff.〕 (in 〔55.9〕 ms. gauṣṭhika, see Speyerʼs note); 〔100.13 ff.〕; MSV 〔ii.78.2〕. Obscure is Mv 〔iii.121.9〕 (vs), in which Śuddhodana addresses the Buddha: purā tuvaṃ goṣṭhika-tūlikāsu …; Senart suggests doubtfully coussins, divans où on est assis de compagnie (tūlikā, mattress, Skt.).

gosāraka (so Mironov also, with v.l. gośălaka), m., an architectural term, acc. to Tib. bcam (gduṅ; cf. Das gduṅ pa, gduṅ ma): Mvy 〔5577〕. The surrounding terms [] seem to refer to parts of a pillar; does this mean a cross-beam, connecting pillars?
